entity: Redwood Fabrication, Inc. — C corporation (assumption; prior returns show a federal NOL carryforward, consistent with corporate filing)
event: Discharge of indebtedness on the plan effective date, in a chapter 11 case (Case No. 26-11842-TBM). Confirmation/effective dates not yet in the file — see QUESTIONS.md.
debt_discharged_computation: Allowed general unsecured claims $8,400,000.00 (plan term sheet) minus plan payments $8,400,000.00 x 35% = $2,940,000.00, leaving $8,400,000.00 - $2,940,000.00 = $5,460,000.00 discharged on the effective date. DIP facility is NOT discharged — repaid in full from exit financing (term sheet), so it generates no COD income. Pre-petition wage claims within the §507(a)(4) cap and the Apex claim were paid during the case (Dkt. 9; Dkt. 48) — also no discharge there.
exclusion_authority: 26 U.S.C. §108(a)(1)(A) (library: irc_108.md) — discharge occurs in a title 11 case, so the entire $5,460,000.00 is excluded from gross income. (The threshold question whether the discharge 'occurs in a title 11 case' is answered by the plan-effective-date discharge in the chapter 11 case; the plan must be confirmed — pending, flagged.)

attribute_reduction.other: None. The excluded amount ($5,460,000.00) is applied first to attribute (A), NOLs, per §108(b)(1) (library: irc_108.md): NOL of $6,100,000.00 at petition (term sheet) minus $5,460,000.00 = $640,000.00 remaining. Arithmetic check: 6,100,000 - 5,460,000 = 640,000 (NOT 650,000). Because the NOL fully absorbs the reduction, attributes (B)-(G) — general business credits, minimum tax credit, capital losses, basis of property ($3.2M in fixed assets per term sheet), passive losses, FTCs — are untouched. Caveat: the $6,100,000 figure is the PETITION-date NOL per prior returns; §108(b) reduces the NOL 'for the year of discharge and carryovers' — any 2026 post-petition NOL year (or two years, 3/10/2026 and the balance of 2026, if a short year applies — short-year rule not in the library, so unverified) would change the starting amount. Flagged as an open item; not forced.

election_108b5: No. Under §108(b)(5) (library: irc_108.md) the taxpayer may elect to apply any portion of the reduction first to basis of depreciable property. Do not elect: (1) the NOL carryforward of $6,100,000.00 already absorbs the entire $5,460,000.00 reduction with $640,000.00 to spare, so the default order costs nothing beyond the attribute reduction itself; (2) depreciable-asset basis is only $3,200,000.00 (term sheet) — an election could not even absorb the full reduction and the remaining $5,460,000.00 - $3,200,000.00 = $2,260,000.00 would spill to other attributes anyway; (3) fresh-start reporting is NOT adopted here (see fresh_start.md — test (b) fails), so the entity keeps its historical asset basis for tax purposes and there is no accounting-basis reset that would make sacrificing tax basis a freebie. Net: preserving NOLs and keeping fixed-asset basis intact is the better position on the facts in the file. (Comparative value of an NOL dollar vs. a basis dollar depends on rates and timing not in the file — labeled unverified; conclusion rests on the arithmetic above, which is sufficient.)
